title: the DSG Battlesystem options underground - the mass-combat adaptation with the narrow frontages, combat/formation/morale modifiers, ventilation, flying, line-of-sight and cave-in rules, plus the R507 chapter tail (the footman pull-down and the stake defenses)

banner.title: The DSG BATTLESYSTEM OPTIONS UNDERGROUND, R508: the printed pp. 34-35 (pdf 35-36) - the opener (battles every bit as common underground, the new tactics, the any-scenario rule), the extremely narrow frontages (the 1/2- and 3/4-inch bottleneck figures), the combat modifiers (the 10% wounded marker vs the standard 25%, with the orc-figure example), the formation modifiers (the column formation, the 1-inch-10-yards scale, the shape-changing figure at twice lengthwise space, the narrower-corridor spacing), the morale effects (the no-room auto-rout and the chain reaction through the blocking friendly unit), the ventilation effects (the doubled gas durations, the wind-carried spell gas at 1/2 the area diameter), the flying effects (the 240/60/30 ceiling bands with the altitude thirds), the line-of-sight effects (the +6 Attack Rating composite of the -4 attacks and damage, the -4 saves, +4 AC vs melee, 1/3 movement, the first-rank obstacle rule, the one-light-per-figure negation, the +2 missile benefit against illuminated units) and the cave-ins (the 6d8 ceiling collapse halved on a save with the 60-dice orc example, the 4d8 mud fall, the 1% base with the +4% cumulative sub-25 increase and the heavy-unit 13-to-26 doubling) - PLUS the R507 chapter tail from the top of printed p. 34: the footman pull-down at -2/-4/-6 by mount speed and the stake defenses (two characters one hour per 10-foot square, the 1d4-1 stakes per 10-foot depth, the chain/plate barding reductions, the 2d6 per stake).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read - every numeric cell dual-confirmed; the three garble classes settled: djvu 648 = 6d8 (proven by the 60-dice orc example at 10 orcs and the 4d8 mud read), djvu 496 = +4% (Acrobat "raised 4%"), djvu 1396 = 13% (Acrobat "13%", doubled to 26%); the dismount tail pins with this round per the content-density rule (it prints on the top of p. 34, past the R507 gap box's pp. 30-33) and CORRECTS the R507 record's "WSG-only -4 pull-down" note - the DSG pull-down is real but speed-band framed (-2/-4/-6) where the WSG pins the flat -4 (wfcGrappleUnmountedPenalty); the +6 Attack Rating is the composite of the R507 dnqDark -4 attacks and damage, verified against rules/dsgfight.h and rules/wsgfight.h const-for-const - NOTHING auto-credited.
banner.sentinel: Pure prose round - no printed grid, no tables, no sentinels. The Battlesystem figure-scale cells pin as inches-to-yards consts (1 inch = 10 yards); the wounded-marker and collapse-chance cells pin as percent consts; the R507 tail pins under the same dnr prefix with the provenance note that it is the R507 chapter's own continuation text.

audit_comment: The DSG Battlesystem options underground pins the dismount tail (the footman pull-down at -2 below 6 inches per round, -4 at 7-12, -6 above 12, the free steed attacks on a fast miss, the -1 per additional footman up to 4, the no-damage multi-person cushion, the eight-man-sized-or-four-large surround, and the stake defenses - gap_flips.from: - [ ] **Battlesystem options underground** (pp. 34-35) - the mass-combat adaptation: narrow frontages, combat modifiers, formation modifiers, morale effects, ventilation effects, flying effects, line-of-sight effects and battlefield cave-ins
gap_flips.to: - [x] **Battlesystem options underground** (pp. 34-35) - the mass-combat adaptation: narrow frontages, combat modifiers, formation modifiers, morale effects, ventilation effects, flying effects, line-of-sight effects and battlefield cave-ins - R508: the Battlesystem chapter in one round - the column-formation rules, the 10% wounded marker, the morale chain reaction, the doubled gas durations, the ceiling-band flight rules, the +6 Attack Rating darkness composite and the cave-in system (with the R507 dismount tail from the top of p. 34: the speed-banded footman pull-down and the stake defenses)
- [x] Extremely narrow frontages (p. 34) - R508: the bottleneck rule - a single 1/2- or 3/4-inch figure holds a gap against a column; modify when only one or two figures face each other
- [x] Combat modifiers (p. 34) - R508: the wounded marker at 10% of the figure's Hit Dice (vs 25% standard), with the orc-figure example (1-9 dice wounds, less than 1 die nothing, 10 or more removes)

- [x] Formation modifiers (p. 34) - R508: the column formation (one figure wide, command radius at the head, no facing-change penalty, open for morale), the 1-inch-10-yards scale, the shape-changing figure doubling its lengthwise space to the back, and the narrower-corridor spacing that doubles column length

- [x] Morale effects (p. 34) - R508: the closed formation without room to expand automatically routs, and a routing formation blocked by a friendly unit routes the blocker - a chain reaction of whatever length required

- [x] Ventilation effects (p. 34) - R508: the doubled poison-gas durations underground (skipped under unusually good circulation), the smoke cross-reference to the p. 36 environment section, and the wind-carried spell gas in a tunnel up to 1/2 the area-of-effect diameter lasting twice the normal duration

- [x] Flying effects (p. 34) - R508: the ceiling bands - 240+ feet normal rules (no upward escape), 60-240 the altitude thirds, 30-60 medium and low evenly divided, under 30 low-level only, maneuverability critical

- [x] Line-of-sight effects (p. 35) - R508: the +6 Attack Rating darkness composite (the -4 attacks and damage of blinded creatures), the -4 saves, +4 AC vs melee, 1/3 movement, the automatic first-rank obstacle hit, the one-light-per-figure negation with the 24-figure example, and the +2 missile benefit against illuminated units that spread-out skirmishers escape

- [x] Cave-ins on a battlefield (p. 35) - R508: the ceiling collapse at 6d8 (halved on a save) with the area plus 1 inch in all directions and the 60-dice orc-figure example, the 4d8 mud fall, and the fragile-formation system - base 1%, the secret d100 check, the +4% cumulative increase per sub-25 survived check, and the doublings for heavy units (13% to 26%), direct spell hits and adjacent collapses

consts.name: dnrPullSlowMaxInches
consts.comment: the pull-down slow band: the steed moving at 6 inches per round or less.

consts.name: dnrPullSlowPenalty
consts.comment: the pull-down attack modifier in the slow band: -2.

consts.name: dnrPullMidMinInches
consts.comment: the pull-down mid band opens at 7 inches per round.

consts.name: dnrPullMidMaxInches
consts.comment: the pull-down mid band ceiling: 12 inches per round.

consts.name: dnrPullMidPenalty
consts.comment: the pull-down attack modifier in the mid band: -4 (the WSG pins a flat -4 for the unmounted pull-down - different framing, pinned as printed).

consts.name: dnrPullFastMinInches
consts.comment: the pull-down fast band opens above 12 inches per round.

consts.name: dnrPullFastPenalty
consts.comment: the pull-down attack modifier in the fast band: -6.

consts.name: dnrPullExtraFootmanMax
consts.comment: each additional footman grappling - up to 4 - applies a penalty to the rider's Proficiency Check.

consts.name: dnrPullExtraFootmanPenalty
consts.comment: the per-additional-footman penalty to the rider's Proficiency Check: -1.

consts.name: dnrPullSurroundManSizedCount
consts.comment: a mount surrounded by eight man-sized creatures can be pulled down with its rider.

consts.name: dnrPullSurroundLargeCount
consts.comment: a mount surrounded by four large creatures can be pulled down with its rider.

consts.name: dnrStakesPrepCharacters
consts.comment: it takes two characters to prepare a staked defensive area.

consts.name: dnrStakesPrepHours
consts.comment: the staked-area preparation time: one hour.

consts.name: dnrStakesAreaFeetSq
consts.comment: the prepared stakes cover a 10-foot-square area.

consts.name: dnrStakesLengthLoFt
consts.comment: the stakes run about four feet in length.

consts.name: dnrStakesLengthHiFt
consts.comment: the stakes run up to about five feet in length.

consts.name: dnrStakesHitDiceMinus
consts.comment: the mount hits 0-3 stakes per 10-foot depth of the defenses: 1d4-1 (one die, minus 1).

consts.name: dnrStakesHitDiceSides
consts.comment: the stakes-hit die: d4.

consts.name: dnrStakesPerDepthFt
consts.comment: the stakes hit per 10-foot-depth of the defenses.

consts.name: dnrStakesBardingChainReduction
consts.comment: chain mail barding reduces the number of stakes that hit by -1.

consts.name: dnrStakesBardingPlateReduction
consts.comment: plate barding reduces the number of stakes that hit by -2.

consts.name: dnrStakeDamageDice
consts.comment: each stake causes 2d6 points of damage to the mount: two dice.

consts.name: dnrStakeDamageSides
consts.comment: the stake damage die: d6.

consts.name: dnrFrontNarrowFigureHalfInch
consts.comment: the narrow bottleneck figures: the 1/2-inch-wide figure denominator (one half inch).

consts.name: dnrFrontNarrowFigureThreeQuarter
consts.comment: the narrow bottleneck figures: the 3/4-inch-wide figure numerator-half (three quarters inch).

consts.name: dnrWoundedThresholdPct
consts.comment: the wounded marker threshold underground: 10% or more of the figure's Hit Dice removed.

consts.name: dnrWoundedStandardPct
consts.comment: the standard-rules wounded marker threshold: 25% or more - the underground rule is stricter.

consts.name: dnrWoundedOrcFigureOrcs
consts.comment: the worked example orc figure represents 10 orcs.

consts.name: dnrWoundedOrcFigureHitDice
consts.comment: the worked example orc figure carries a total of 10 Hit Dice.

consts.name: dnrWoundedOrcWoundedLoDice
consts.comment: the orc figure is marked wounded if an attack inflicts 1-9 dice of damage: the floor 1.

consts.name: dnrWoundedOrcWoundedHiDice
consts.comment: the wounded-band ceiling in the orc example: 9 dice of damage still only wounds.

consts.name: dnrWoundedRemovedDice
consts.comment: an attack inflicting 10 or more dice removes the figure.

consts.name: dnrScaleInchYards
consts.comment: the Battlesystem game scale: 1 inch equals 10 yards.

consts.name: dnrFigureLengthwiseMult
consts.comment: the tight-confines figure occupies twice as much space lengthwise as it normally would.

consts.name: dnrVentGasDurationMult
consts.comment: the duration of all poisonous gases is DOUBLED when released underground.

consts.name: dnrVentSmokeRefPage
consts.comment: the smoke-effects cross-reference: the Underground Environment section on printed p. 36.

consts.name: dnrVentSpellGasMaxDiameterFrac
consts.comment: the wind-carry case requires a tunnel or passageway no more than 1/2 the diameter of the spell's area of effect (denominator 2).

consts.name: dnrFlyNormalMinCeilingFt
consts.comment: a ceiling of 240 feet or higher uses the normal Battlesystem flight rules.

consts.name: dnrFlyThirdsMinCeilingFt
consts.comment: the thirds mapping opens at a ceiling of 60 feet.

consts.name: dnrFlyTwoBandMinCeilingFt
consts.comment: the two-altitude band opens above a 30-foot ceiling.

consts.name: dnrLosArPenalty
consts.comment: creatures without infravision fighting in darkness suffer a +6 penalty to the unit's Attack Rating.

consts.name: dnrLosSavePenalty
consts.comment: the saving throws of individuals unable to see suffer a -4 penalty.

consts.name: dnrLosAcMeleePenalty
consts.comment: the Armor Class of the creatures is raised by four against all melee attacks.

consts.name: dnrLosMoveMultDen
consts.comment: the movement rating of a unit that cannot see is reduced to 1/3 of its original (denominator 3).

consts.name: dnrLosLightExampleFigures
consts.comment: the worked example: in a unit of 24 figures, at least 24 individuals must be equipped with torches or magical lights.

consts.name: dnrLosLitMissileArBonus
consts.comment: if missiles are fired against the illuminated unit, the Attack Rating of the missile-using troops receives a +2 benefit in addition to any other modifiers that apply.

consts.name: dnrCaveinPlusInches
consts.comment: the ground area expansion of a ceiling collapse: plus 1 inch in all directions.

consts.name: dnrCaveinDamageDice
consts.comment: a ceiling collapse deals 6d8 hit points of damage to all creatures in the area of effect: six dice (the djvu 648 garble, settled by the 60-dice orc example and the 4d8 mud read).

consts.name: dnrCaveinDamageSides
consts.comment: the ceiling-collapse damage die: d8.

consts.name: dnrCaveinOrcFigureDice
consts.comment: the worked-example collapse damage on the 10-orc figure: 60 dice.

consts.name: dnrCaveinMudDamageDice
consts.comment: a similar weight of falling mud deals only 4d8 points of damage.

consts.name: dnrCaveinMudDamageSides
consts.comment: the falling-mud damage die: d8.

consts.name: dnrCaveinBasePct
consts.comment: the base chance of a frail feature collapsing is 1% whenever marching or melee combat occurs nearby.

consts.name: dnrCaveinCumulativeRollBelow
consts.comment: if a formation is checked once and does not collapse, but the resulting d100 roll was less than 25, the collapse chance rises.

consts.name: dnrCaveinCumulativePlusPct
consts.comment: the cumulative collapse-chance increase per sub-25 survived check: +4% (the djvu 496 garble, Acrobat "raised 4%").

consts.name: dnrCaveinHeavyExamplePct
consts.comment: the worked example: a bridge with a 13% chance of collapse (the djvu 1396 garble, Acrobat 13%).

consts.name: dnrCaveinHeavyExampleDoubledPct
consts.comment: the worked example doubled: the 13% bridge has a 26% chance if a heavy cavalry unit gallops over it.

bools.name: dnrFootmanPullManSizedOnly
bools.comment: characters and creatures on foot can attempt to pull a rider from his horse - but only creatures that are man-sized or larger.

bools.name: dnrFootmanPullLargerCountTwoMen
bools.comment: creatures larger than man-size count as two men for the pull attempt.

bools.name: dnrFootmanGrabAsPasses
bools.comment: the character on foot must first grab the rider as he passes by, with an attack roll modified by the speed of the mount.

bools.name: dnrPullHitFollowsGrappleProcedure
bools.comment: a successful pull-down hit follows the same procedure as if the rider had been grappled by a mounted opponent.

bools.name: dnrPullMissFastFreeAttacks
bools.comment: on a missed pull-down attempt with the steed moving faster than 12 inches per round, the steed gets a free set of attacks against the character on foot.

bools.name: dnrPullMultiPersonNoDamage
bools.comment: a rider pulled from his mount by more than one person suffers no damage - his opponents actually cushion his fall.

bools.name: dnrPullBothMountAndRider
bools.comment: the surrounded case pulls down both the mount and the rider.

bools.name: dnrPullBothKeepNormalAttacks
bools.comment: during this combat both the mount and the rider are allowed their normal attacks.

bools.name: dnrSetDefensesPreparable
bools.comment: given time and material, set defenses can be prepared to dismount riders and stop horses.

bools.name: dnrSetDefensesSimpleTricks
bools.comment: most of the set defenses are simple tricks and traps - a rope hung between two columns at the rider's height, a trip wire, etc.

bools.name: dnrSetDefensesDmChance
bools.comment: the DM determines the chance of success for these types of traps.

bools.name: dnrStakesSharpened
bools.comment: for defense against mounted attackers, sharpened stakes can be set in the ground.

bools.name: dnrStakesNeedSaplings
bools.comment: the stakes require a supply of saplings, light wood, or spears.

bools.name: dnrStakesEasilySpotted
bools.comment: the defensive areas are easily spotted and can be avoided if there is an alternate route.

bools.name: dnrStakesEnterHorsemanshipCheck
bools.comment: a rider who wishes his mount to enter a staked area must make a horsemanship Proficiency Check, just as if trying a jump or leap.

bools.name: dnrStakesCheckFailRefuses
bools.comment: a failed check means the mount refuses to enter the area, although it continues moving in another direction if possible.

bools.name: dnrStakesCheckSuccessEnters
bools.comment: a successful check means the mount enters the defended area.

bools.name: dnrStakeDamageChargingOrNot
bools.comment: the stake damage applies whether or not the steed was charging at the time.

bools.name: dnrBsBattlesCommonUnderground
bools.comment: battles are every bit as common underground as on the surface - armed expeditions to the underearth, or subterranean races vying for control of key tunnel sections.

bools.name: dnrBsMassCombatInstrument
bools.comment: mass combat can be an instrument of every underground campaign.

bools.name: dnrBsConstrictedNewTactics
bools.comment: the constricted nature of the underground environment demands a whole new set of tactics for warfare in the underearth.

bools.name: dnrBsDarknessFlyingNovel
bools.comment: darkness and restrictions on flying create situations not commonly encountered above ground.

bools.name: dnrBsForUnderearthBattlefields
bools.comment: the optional Battlesystem rules are designed for the unusual battlefields of the underearth.

bools.name: dnrBsClarifiesIndoorWarfare
bools.comment: the rules also serve to clarify other types of combat, such as indoor or house-to-house warfare.

bools.name: dnrBsAnyScenarioIfAllAgree
bools.comment: if all players are agreeable, the rules can be employed during any Battlesystem scenario.

bools.name: dnrFrontBottleneckHoldsGap
bools.comment: underground battlefields often possess terrain bottlenecks that allow a single figure to hold a gap against a long column of attackers.

bools.name: dnrFrontDesignedSeveralFigures
bools.comment: the Battlesystem rules are designed for combat between several figures at a time.

bools.name: dnrFrontModifyOneOrTwo
bools.comment: the rules should be modified if only one or two figures face each other in combat.

bools.name: dnrWoundedStricterThanStandard
bools.comment: the underground wounded threshold is stricter than the standard 25%.

bools.name: dnrWoundedBelowOneDieNoEffect
bools.comment: an attack inflicting less than one die of damage does not affect the figure.

bools.name: dnrColTunnelsForceColumns
bools.comment: movement through winding tunnels and narrow passages is difficult for military units in formation - such units generally move as long, thin columns.

bools.name: dnrColOneFigureWide
bools.comment: a column formation displays as a line of figures, one figure wide and as long as the number of figures in the unit.

bools.name: dnrColCommandRadiusAtHead
bools.comment: a column is in its leader's command radius when the figure at its head is in the leader's command radius.

bools.name: dnrColNoFacingPenalty
bools.comment: a column pays no movement penalty for changing facing - as the tunnel winds, the column winds with it and still moves a distance equal to its movement rating.

bools.name: dnrColOpenForMorale
bools.comment: a unit in column formation is considered in open formation for purposes of morale checks.

bools.name: dnrScaleHalflingCannotOccupy
bools.comment: at the game scale not even a 1/2-inch halfling or kobold figure could normally occupy a 10-foot-wide corridor.

bools.name: dnrFigureChangesShape
bools.comment: the individual creatures can still fit into the area, so the figure is assumed to change its shape to fit the tight confines.

bools.name: dnrFigureOccupiesMoreFrontToBack
bools.comment: the figure actually occupies more space front to back than it does from side to side.

bools.name: dnrFigureExtraSpaceToBack
bools.comment: the extra space is always considered to lie to the back of the figure.

bools.name: dnrFigureAdjacentInFront
bools.comment: a 3/4-inch figure in a 1/3-inch corridor can be placed adjacent to an enemy figure in front of it.

bools.name: dnrFigureRearApproachLimit
bools.comment: if another figure, friendly or enemy, approaches from the rear, it can only move to within 3/4 inch of the original figure.

bools.name: dnrColNarrowerFiguresSpread
bools.comment: if a column or portion thereof occupies a corridor narrower than its figures, the figures must be placed twice as far apart as normal.

bools.name: dnrColNarrowerDoublesLength
bools.comment: the twice-as-far-apart placement doubles the length of the column.

bools.name: dnrMoraleClosedBreaksHarmful
bools.comment: units in closed formation can suffer harmful morale effects if forced to break into open formation where they lack sufficient room.

bools.name: dnrMoraleExpandSidesFrontRear
bools.comment: a closed formation unit forced to break open can expand to the sides, or to the front or rear.

bools.name: dnrMoraleNoRoomAutoRouts
bools.comment: a closed formation unit without enough space to expand fully in at least one direction automatically routs.

bools.name: dnrMoraleRoutingBlockedRoutesBlocker
bools.comment: if a routing formation is prohibited from performing its routing movement by the presence of a friendly unit - no possible retreat path around it - the unit blocking the path of retreat is automatically routed.

bools.name: dnrMoraleChainReaction
bools.comment: the automatic routing can turn into a chain reaction of whatever length is required to clear a path for the routing units.

bools.name: dnrVentGoodCirculationSkip
bools.comment: if an underground battlefield has unusually good air circulation by natural or manufactured means, the ventilation rule should not be used.

bools.name: dnrVentAirSlowerUnderground
bools.comment: in most cases air circulates much more slowly underground than in the outside world - gases and smoke take much longer to disperse.

bools.name: dnrVentSmokeMajorProblem
bools.comment: the smoke caused by fires can create a major problem underground (see the Underground Environment section, printed p. 36).

bools.name: dnrVentSpellGasWindCarried
bools.comment: a gaseous spell effect in a windy but relatively small area can be moved by the wind and still retain its potency.

bools.name: dnrVentWindCarryDurationDoubled
bools.comment: wind blowing through the cave does not disperse the gas until twice the normal duration of the gas.

bools.name: dnrVentWindCarryAffectsPath
bools.comment: the carried gas affects all susceptible creatures in its path.

bools.name: dnrFlyLargeCavernsAllowFlight
bools.comment: while the dimensions of many underground battlefields prohibit flying creatures, certain extraordinary caverns and realms are large enough to allow flight.

bools.name: dnrFlyMayNotEscapeUpward
bools.comment: even with a normal-rules ceiling, a flying creature might not be able to escape the battlefield by flying up and away.

bools.name: dnrFlyThirdsMapping
bools.comment: between 60 and 240 feet use the normal low, medium and high designations, altered so low covers the bottom third, medium the middle third, and high the upper third of the available flying space.

bools.name: dnrFlyTwoBandOnly
bools.comment: a ceiling greater than 30 but less than 60 feet uses only medium and low altitudes, evenly divided between the two elevations.

bools.name: dnrFlyLowOnlyUnderThirty
bools.comment: ceilings lower than 30 feet allow only low-level flying creatures to take flight.

bools.name: dnrFlyManeuverabilityCritical
bools.comment: flying underground is very tricky and maneuverability is critical.

bools.name: dnrLosBlackerThanNightBattles
bools.comment: a battle fought in the inky blackness of the underearth suffers vision effects even more extreme than those listed for Night Battles - Battlesystem game case 12.5.

bools.name: dnrLosNeedFireMagicPhosphorescence
bools.comment: unless fire, magical light, or a patch of phosphorescence somehow illuminates the field, creatures without infravision are at a great disadvantage.

bools.name: dnrLosArCompositesAttacksDamage
bools.comment: the +6 Attack Rating penalty reflects the combined effects of the -4 to attacks and -4 damage applied to blinded creatures (the R507 dnqDark numbers).

bools.name: dnrLosObstacleFirstRankAuto
bools.comment: if a unit unable to see encounters an unexpected obstacle such as a pit, pool of mud, or anything else that could trap the leading rank, the entire first rank of the unit is automatically affected.

bools.name: dnrLosObstaclePushExplanation
bools.comment: the first-rank rule accounts for the fact that even at the slowed rate, the front individuals cannot communicate the obstacle before the ranks behind push them into it.

bools.name: dnrLosOneLightPerFigure
bools.comment: at least one light source must be employed for each figure in the unit to negate the darkness penalties.

bools.name: dnrLosLitMovesNormal
bools.comment: a unit carrying its light source moves at its normal rate.

bools.name: dnrLosLitMeleesNormal
bools.comment: the illuminated unit performs melee attacks normally.

bools.name: dnrLosLitSavesNormal
bools.comment: the illuminated unit makes saving throws with the usual percentage chance of success.

bools.name: dnrLosLitNoMissilesAtUnseen
bools.comment: the illuminated unit cannot fire missiles at targets it cannot see.

bools.name: dnrLosLitNoChargeBeyondVision
bools.comment: the illuminated unit cannot initiate a charge against a unit out of its range of vision.

bools.name: dnrLosLitEasilySeen
bools.comment: a unit thus illuminated is easily seen by all forces on the field.

bools.name: dnrSkirmishersIlluminateTargets
bools.comment: skirmishers can advance before a formation with torches, illuminating an enemy unit or target, or marking the terrain for a unit soon to come that way.

bools.name: dnrSkirmishersNoLitPenalty
bools.comment: because they are spread so, skirmishers with torches do not suffer the +2 penalty against them when fired at with missile weapons.

bools.name: dnrCaveinSpellsHighDemand
bools.comment: spells and effects that bring the massive weight of stone crashing down on foes are in high demand underground - the damage wrought by a collapse is devastating.

bools.name: dnrCaveinEarthquakeCommon
bools.comment: earthquake and transmute rock to mud are commonly used to bring down ceilings.

bools.name: dnrCaveinAreaPlusInch
bools.comment: if a ceiling collapses, the area affected on the ground is the same as the area of the ceiling collapsed, plus 1 inch in all directions.

bools.name: dnrCaveinSaveHalves
bools.comment: a saving throw vs. spell reduces the collapse damage to half.

bools.name: dnrCaveinOrcFigureDestroyed
bools.comment: the worked example: the 10-orc figure suffers 60 dice of damage and is automatically destroyed whether it saves or not.

bools.name: dnrCaveinMudSaveHalves
bools.comment: the mud-fall damage is again halved if the saving throw is successful.

bools.name: dnrCaveinUnstableDmDiscretion
bools.comment: unstable bridges, ledges, or other rock formations subject to unusual stress when heavy creatures move across or next to them are left to the DM's discretion.

bools.name: dnrCaveinColumnsArchesCracked
bools.comment: along with bridges and ledges, the collapse of narrow columns or arches - even worn and cracked sections of cavern ceilings - can be catastrophic.

bools.name: dnrCaveinSpellsTrigger
bools.comment: spells such as lightning bolt or earthquake can also trigger the collapse.

bools.name: dnrCaveinSecretCheck
bools.comment: the DM or neutral referee should make a secret d100 check whenever stress is applied to a fragile formation.

bools.name: dnrCaveinCumulativeEffect
bools.comment: the cumulative increase means the feature could grow increasingly fragile as the battle continues.

bools.name: dnrCaveinHeavyUnitsDouble
bools.comment: the presence of heavy units - heavy cavalry, chariots, or large creatures - doubles the chance of a collapse.

bools.name: dnrCaveinDirectSpellHitDoubles
bools.comment: the formation's chance of collapsing doubles if an explosive spell such as a lightning bolt strikes it directly.

bools.name: dnrCaveinAdjacentCollapseDoubles
bools.comment: the chance also doubles if an earthquake or similar effect causes the rock immediately adjacent to the threatened area to collapse.
